content: Always disclose product availability early to avoid surprising the customer after building excitement.
For technical customers, prioritize live demos and hands-on testing over verbal explanations.
Use specific technical metrics (e.g., 1.3mm key travel, sub-1ms latency) to build credibility with knowledgeable users.
When a product is not available locally, have a clear reservation or pre-order process ready to convert interest into a commitment.

name: Live Demo Immersion
condition: When the customer requests a feature demonstration, especially for technical products.
example: Customer asks to see VS Code in desktop mode. Salesperson immediately opens the app and lets the customer interact.

name: Hands-On Validation
condition: When the customer is skeptical about performance claims.
example: Customer wants to test key travel. Salesperson invites them to type and run a script to feel the latency.

name: Early Availability Disclosure
condition: When the product is not yet launched in the customer's market.
example: At the start of the interaction, say: 'This model is coming soon to Turkey. Let me show you what it can do, and I can reserve one for you.'

rebuttal_template: I understand your concern. While the MatePad Air isn't officially launched in Turkey yet, I can offer you a priority reservation for the first batch. In the meantime, let me show you the full capabilities on this demo unit so you can be confident in your decision.

I see that price is a concern. Let me show you how the desktop mode and low-latency keyboard can replace a laptop, saving you from buying a separate device. Plus, with the included M-Pencil and WPS, you're getting a complete productivity suite.

I understand you're comparing specs. Let me set up a side-by-side demo with the competitor's device so you can see the real-world performance difference, especially in multitasking and keyboard latency.
